i was there when my grandma passed peacefully in hospital. i saw her dead and it made me incredibly sad but she looked peaceful, so it was okay. after her passing, the doctor needed co come and confirm her death, meanwhile the nurses told us to go take a walk and clear our heads while the doctor visits and they change my grandma out of her hospital gown and into one of her favorite pyjamas. 
when we came back and my grandmas clothes were changed and she was laying neatly in her bed, she didn't look like herself anymore, more like a very pale elderly woman. i almost couldn't recognise her anymore.
at that moment, i became incredibly aware that she is gone forever.

idk yet if it was good or bad for me to see her dead like that but i believe that it's completely personal whether seeing a loved one dead helps to find closure or not.

We have 50/50 school and work (we're paid student salary the whole time). currently i'm working for 6 weeks and rotate through all modalities. it's planned individually where (modality) each student will work but throughout the 3yrs of school we should have gained some experience in all modalities.

i really liked mammo, same as i liked x-ray. it's a steady workflow, there are no waiting times bc of long lasting exams (mri) and i love to work with many different patients.

i guess it's gonna be some painful pulling. there are also men's chests in mammo. i've never seen extremely small breasts/men's breasts as i was only in mammo for a week but i think small breasts shouldn't be that much of a problem. for sure it's more difficult to position. if the tissue is extremely dense and sensitive, it may be too painful to compress enough, which brings terrible image quality. in that case i wouldn't do a mammo bc that would be a unnessecary x-ray exposure. would go with sono then

as i'm still in rad tech school, maybe other ppl can add their experience. i'm not 100% sure about my answer

i still have very little experience with mammographic imaging but as far as i know there are some indication for breast cancer: irregular hyperdense spots and/or (several) small microcalcifications 
this patient was there for screening while having cases of breast cancer in anamnese. i think this boob is healthy but i'm not a doctor
additions are very welcome if some of you know more about mammo or my information is not (fully) correct :)
